An archaeologist travels with the group and uses the Sultanate monuments of Delhi, Mughal Agra and Fatehpur Sikri, and eighteenth-century Jaipur to show how three courts planned and built their capitals.

A day-by-day itinerary and a quotation are shared before you commit. Route, pace, accommodation and budget are adjusted to suit your group.

What it covers

  • Delhi: the monuments of the Sultanate
  • Agra and Fatehpur Sikri: the Mughal court
  • Jaipur: a planned city of the eighteenth century
  • An archaeologist with the group throughout

Day by day

  1. Day 1: Sultanate Delhi

    The Qutb complex and Mehrauli: how Delhi's first Sultanate capitals were built.

  2. Day 2: Mughal Delhi

    Humayun's Tomb in the morning; the Red Fort and the streets of Shahjahanabad in the afternoon.

  3. Day 3: Agra

    Drive to Agra. Agra Fort, and the Taj Mahal from across the river at sunset.

  4. Day 4: The Taj Mahal and Fatehpur Sikri

    The Taj Mahal at opening, then Akbar's city at Fatehpur Sikri on the way to Jaipur.

  5. Day 5: Jaipur

    Amber Fort, the City Palace and Jantar Mantar: a planned city of the eighteenth century.

  6. Day 6: Departure or an extra day

    A museum, a second fort, or a slower start before you leave.

Days can be added, removed or reordered. The final itinerary comes with your quotation.

You take away

Daily field sheets and a final comparative portfolio.
